input.question: When the Rocky Mountains are old enough that they look like the Appalachians, what will the Appalachians look like?
input.ground_truth: Rolling hills and eventually plains, you are correct. The highest points of Earth are constantly being eroded towards the lowest places on Earth. The Precambrian rocky mountains (~1 billion years ago) were worn completely flat before the current uplift (80 million some years old) created the current rocky mountains. An example of the Precambrian Rockies can be found in Pikes Peak Granite as a pink crumbly rock. _URL_0_

But if you leave it there for a long, long time, the waves and wind will make it shorter and rounder, until it looks like a little hill—kind of like the gentle, rounded hills of the Appalachians.

So, when the Rocky Mountains get old and become short and rounded like the Appalachians now, the old Appalachians will have become even smaller and flatter! They will look like just flat land, because they are even older and have been worn down a lot by rain, wind, and time.

So, just like your sandcastle turns into a little bump and then disappears, the mountains get smaller and flatter as they get older!
